why: A qualifier rule is only as wide as its scope. The scope is written here, next to the exclusions and their reasons, so a reader sees which machine-readable artefacts the rule covers instead of inferring it from globs in code.

exclude.reason: superseded signed artefacts retained verbatim (the r19 reader receipts v1). The current receipts are in receipts/reader/ and are in scope; this directory is history, not a claim.
superseded revision records (r12-r19). History is retained verbatim and is not relabelled; the current revision's gate is GATE_R20.json and it is in scope.
owner rulings for superseded revisions; a ruling is the owner's words and editing it would rewrite the record. Current ruling: out/OWNER_RULING_W0_R20.json.
the r12 board, superseded by out/KANBAN_R20.json which is in scope.
the r15 board, superseded by out/KANBAN_R20.json which is in scope.
the r12 acceptance record, superseded by out/ACCEPTANCE_R20.json which is in scope.
a rebuildable copy of out/, receipts/ and evidence/; scanning it double-counts rather than widening.
other lanes' verbatim verdict text and briefs; the author may quote a lane but must not relabel it.
the independent officer's own artefacts, kept as received.
